bugs.text: The player's ship never appears. player.alive starts false, the only assignment to true is inside the respawn branch (470) that needs respawnTimer, which is set only in loseShip (306), which needs a living player. beginStagePlay (282) does nothing for a dead player. As a result the fighter is never drawn, never moves, never fires, dives never launch (gated on p.alive at 558), no enemy can be killed, the stage can never be cleared and GAME OVER can never happen. All play screenshots show an idle formation, no player and score 0.

Challenging stage soft-locks: updateChallenge reads state.wave and state.waveT (undefined; the fields are state.chal.wave/waveT), so spawnWave is never called, chal.wave stays 0 and the end condition chal.wave>=5 is never met. Even with the player fixed, stage 3 would hang on an empty screen.
SND.enemyHit is defined but never called; there is no separate 'enemy hit' sound.
Boss frame 0 row 0 is 14 characters while the other rows are 16; drawSprite uses map[0].length as the width, so the right two columns of every boss row are clipped and the boss is drawn off-centre.
Zako rows are 8 and 12 instead of two rows of 10.
Player-shot vs enemy test allows +2 px above and below the sprite half-height, so enemies are hit over 11 px of height for 7 px sprites (hitbox larger than the sprite).
The formation keeps swaying (amplitude 1.5) after it is complete instead of only breathing.
A freed captive when the player is dead drifts downward forever and state.captured is never cleared, which permanently blocks further tractor-beam dives for that game.

Escorts snap back to 'join' the moment the leader enters the beam state (L.state!=='dive'), so a boss never arrives at its beam with escorts and the 800/1600 values apply only while the boss is still mid-dive.
A boss in 'reenter' (flying back to its slot from the top) scores as diving (400+), not the arcade's formation value.

summary: The file is tidy and compact: a clean fixed-timestep loop, clear state/update/render split, pixel sprites, Web Audio synthesis, a proper title score table, starfield, HUD with reserve ships and denomination flags, curved looping entry paths, sway and breathe, and reasonably complete code for dives, escorts, the tractor beam, capture, rescue, dual fighter, hostile captive, challenging stages and results. On paper it reads like a faithful Galaga. But one initialization bug makes all of it moot: the player's fighter is never set alive at the start of a game, so it is never drawn, cannot move or fire, enemies never dive (that is gated on the player being alive), nothing can be killed and the game sits forever on a completed formation at 0 points, which is exactly what every play screenshot shows. The challenging stage has a second independent soft-lock (wrong state fields for the wave timer). What the player actually experiences is a title screen, a STAGE 1 banner, an enemy fly-in, and then an idle screen; the automated test's moves=true is not confirmed by the code or the frames. Scored strictly, only the presentation, entry choreography and infrastructure earn credit.
